page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate that the t3a.xlarge is designed for workloads with variable CPU utilization. In compute-heavy tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, both single-core and multi-core performance fall into the bottom 10% category. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only large block transfers reaching 23.87 GB/sec. However, the processor demonstrates average performance in the Passmark CPU encryption test, scoring 3207.35, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA-NI instruction sets.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the burstable CPU allocation model allows for a lower-cost hardware profile suitable for environments that do not require continuous high CPU utilization. Because the instance relies on CPU credits to burst above its baseline, it is best suited for low-traffic web servers, small databases, development and testing environments, and background task processing where resource demands are intermittent.
